title: Expression / Functional Indexes in PostgreSQL
realWorldScenario: Users are searching for emails case-insensitively: `WHERE LOWER(email) = 'alex@example.com'`. Even though a B-Tree index exists on `email`, PostgreSQL executes a slow Sequential Scan.
questionStatement: Why does wrapping a column in a function like `LOWER(email)` invalidate a standard B-Tree index? How does an Expression Index solve this problem?
expectedConcepts: Function wrapping prevents standard B-Tree index usage
Expression index DDL syntax: CREATE INDEX ... ON table (FUNCTION(column))
Pre-computation of function outputs in the index
hints: The index stores raw values, but the query tests computed values.
